problem:
$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & b \\ b & c\end{aligned}]
$$

The matrix of the quadratic form $Q(x)={x}_{1}^{2}-6{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}\,$ is given above. What is the value of $b+c?$

feedback.problem:
$$
[\begin{aligned}a & 1 & b \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ b & 0 & c\end{aligned}]
$$

The matrix of the quadratic form $Q(x)=3{x}_{1}^{2}+2{x}_{1}{x}_{2}-10{x}_{1}{x}_{3}+3{x}_{3}^{2}$ is given above. What is the value of $a+b+c?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Since the matrix of the quadratic form must be symmetric, we rewrite our expression as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & =3{x}_{1}^{2}+2{x}_{1}{x}_{2}-10{x}_{1}{x}_{3}+3{x}_{3}^{2} \\  & =3{x}_{1}^{2}+1{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+(-5){x}_{1}{x}_{3} \\  & +\,1{x}_{2}{x}_{1}+0{x}_{2}^{2}+0{x}_{2}{x}_{3} \\  & +\,(-5){x}_{3}{x}_{1}+0{x}_{3}{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that to get a symmetric matrix, we must do the following splits:

- we split the coefficient of $2{x}_{1}{x}_{2}$ between the entries ${a}_{12}={a}_{21}=\frac{2}{2}=1,$ and

- we split the coefficient of $-10{x}_{1}{x}_{3}$ between the entries ${a}_{13}={a}_{31}=\frac{-10}{2}=-5.$

So, the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form is

$$
[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & -5 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ -5 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, $a=3,$ $b=-5,$ and $c=3.$ Finally, 

$$
a+b+c=3+(-5)+3=1.
$$
